papers.title: Mechanical Performance of Functionally Graded Lattice Structures Made with Selective Laser Melting 3D Printing
papers.abstract: The selective laser melting (SLM) process is a metal-based 3D printing technology which is capable of fabricating cellular structures for various engineering applications. This study aims to investigate the compressive mechanical performance and energy absorption capability of uniform and functionally graded lattice structures fabricated using this process. A solution heat treatment was carried out to explore its effect on the mechanical properties of the printed Al-Si12 lattice structures. The as-built condition of SLM lattice structures underwent brittle failure and demonstrated nonideal energy absorption behaviours, while heat treatment was found to significantly improve deformation and energy absorption performance. The deformation behaviour of the heat-treated lattice structure exhibited distinct responses with typical stress strain curves, providing ideal compressive regions. Calculation of energy absorption showed that the gradually denser lattice structure absorbed higher levels of energy than the uniform lattice structure.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the compressive mechanical performance and energy absorption of functionally graded lattice structures produced by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Compression tests were performed on as-built and heat-treated Al-Si12 lattice structures with uniform and graded architectures.
summary_en.result: Heat treatment transformed brittle failure into ductile behavior with ideal stress-strain curves, and graded lattices exhibited superior energy absorption compared to uniform ones.
summary_en.validation: Experimental compression testing with stress-strain curves and energy absorption calculations.

papers.title: Nano-mechanical Behavior of H13 Tool Steel Fabricated by a Selective Laser Melting Method
papers.abstract: Abstract Nano-mechanical properties of selective laser melted H13 steel at a scan laser speed of 100 mm/s were investigated using nanoindentation tests. The findings shed light on the interrelationship between the nanoindentation strain rate and hardness. It was found that the strain-rate sensitivity exponent ( m = 0.022) of this material indicated that the nanoindentation hardness increased in a range of (8.41 to 9.18) GPa with an increase in the strain rate ranging from 0.002 to 0.1 s −1 .

papers.title: Can Functional Assessment Tools Reflect Balance Abilities at 3 Months after Total hip Arthroplasty?
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: This study was conducted to determine if the Harrison hip score (HHS), a tool for assessing hip joint function, and the Burg balance scale (BBS), a general balance assessment tool, actually reflect the balance ability of total hip arthroplasty (THA) patients 3 months after surgery. In addition, this study investigated the initial weight distribution strategy for bilateral lower extremity after THA surgery to understand the balance of THA patients. METHODS: Fourteen 3-month THA patients performed static dual standing and sit-to-stand (STS) tasks. Ground reaction forces on each leg were collected to calculate the weight distribution symmetricity (SWD), and the HHS, functional HHS (f-HHS), and BBS were evaluated.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估功能量表能否反映THA术后3个月的平衡能力。
summary_zh.method: 收集14名THA患者的双下肢地面反力及HHS/BBS评分。
summary_zh.result: HHS和BBS与平衡指标相关性弱，患者采用非移动策略补偿。
summary_zh.validation: 临床观察研究，无实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: The study investigated whether functional assessment tools (HHS and BBS) reflect balance abilities in THA patients at 3 months post-surgery.
summary_en.method: Ground reaction forces during static standing and sit-to-stand tasks were collected from 14 THA patients, and HHS, functional HHS, and BBS were evaluated.
summary_en.result: Weak correlations were found between assessment scores and balance measures, with patients adopting an initial non-movement compensation strategy.
summary_en.validation: This is a clinical observational study without experimental or mechanical validation.
